display.title: Episode 32: King David's Grave (The Three Weeks)
display.summary_short: A king's royal sword falls into the sealed cave of Dovid HaMelech's grave; no one comes back alive until a rabbi goes down after his community says Tehillim. Plus a letter from a boy's yetzer tov.
display.summary_long: Broadcast in the first week of the Three Weeks, with no music. Uncle Yossi opens with a call for achdus: when we show unity and Ahavas Yisroel, as we say in davening, 'bless us, our Father, all of us as one', Hashem sends His blessings, above all Moshiach. He explains the Three Weeks from the 17th of Tammuz to Tisha B'Av. The story tells of a king visiting Yerushalayim who finds that the cave of Dovid HaMelech's grave is sealed because those who enter do not come out alive. Lowering a candle to peer in, he drops his priceless heirloom sword through the bars. Two servants sent down never return. The king asks the local rabbi, who first gathers his community to recite all of Tehillim, then is lowered into the cave and comes back with the sword, having seen only a brilliant light. He tells the king to thank Hashem, and the king grants the Jews freedom to keep the Torah. An eleven-year-old yeshiva student leads the Shema before the story's second half, and the mailbox features an eight-year-old's Yiddish letter written by his yetzer tov to his yetzer hara.
display.lesson: Unity and Ahavas Yisroel bring Hashem's blessings; Tehillim and trust in Hashem protect us, and Dovid HaMelech lives on.

date.note: 'Beginning last Thursday the Three Weeks have begun' (17 Tammuz fell on Thursday 8 July 1982). Matches the weekly estimate.

advisories.note: Two servants lowered into the cave die; others before them never came out alive.

privacy.note: Shema guest and a letter writer named in full on air.

sources_cited.note: 'Bless us, our Father, all of us as one.'
'Dovid, king of Israel, lives on', introduced as 'what is written'.
